{
  "rules": [
    "If sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices — reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.",
    "If sentiment is strongly bearish (≤ -0.50), model underestimates — increase forecast by 1–3% to account for reversal.",
    "After a sharp price spike (≥ 5% from prior peak), model often overshoots — cap forecast at +3% above peak for next 3–5 days.",
    "When true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70), model tends to lag — adjust forecast downward by 1–2% per day until trend stabilizes.",
    "If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.00–0.33), model often fails to capture volatility — add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast to account for hidden risk.",
    "For 30-day horizon, if model forecast is flat or rising slowly while sentiment is volatile, reduce forecast slope by 20–40% to reflect sentiment uncertainty.",
    "If true outcome deviates > 5% from model in first 5 days, model is likely misaligned — re-calibrate using sentiment-weighted moving average of last 7 days."
  ]
}
